passages.text: It is thought a disgrace to love unrequited. But the great will see that true love cannot be unrequited. True love transcends the unworthy object and dwells and broods on the eternal, and when the poor interposed mask crumbles, it is not sad, but feels rid of so much earth and feels its independency the surer.
passages.note: Unrequited love; love that is not returned

passages.text: Rings and other jewels are not gifts, but apologies for gifts. The only gift is a portion of thyself. Thou must bleed for me.
passages.note: Giving something of yourself, not just things

passages.text: No services are of any value, but only likeness. When I have attempted to join myself to others by services, it proved an intellectual trick⁠—no more. They eat your service like apples, and leave you out. But love them, and they feel you and delight in you all the time.
passages.note: Trying to earn belonging by being useful
Hardship as the path of the courageous
